blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Digital transformation of logistics, at senior level, is not about installing new systems — it is about redesigning the flows of information so that decisions become faster, earlier, and better supported by evidence. The technology is only the visible layer. Underneath it sit harder questions about data quality, organisational trust, and the willingness of experienced people to accept a number they did not calculate themselves.

A good transformation has three ingredients. First, a clear view of which decisions actually become significantly better with more and faster data — not all of them do. Second, an honest assessment of the organisation's ability to use that data, which is almost always lower than senior leaders believe. Third, long patience: most logistics transformations take years to pay off, and the ones that try to rush the timeline tend to fail quietly and expensively.

Done well, the result is not dramatic. It is an operation that feels slightly calmer, slightly faster, and slightly more accurate every year. Done badly, it is a museum of expensive software that nobody uses — and a warning to the next generation of leaders.

items.q: According to the text, digital transformation of logistics is primarily about…
options: redesigning how information flows so decisions improve
reducing the size of the operations team
items.why: "it is about redesigning the flows of information so that decisions become faster, earlier, and better supported by evidence."

items.q: What does the author say about the organisation's ability to use data?
options: It is usually higher than expected
It is almost always lower than senior leaders believe
It matters less than the technology chosen
items.why: "an honest assessment of the organisation's ability to use that data, which is almost always lower than senior leaders believe."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Rushing the timeline tends to end in expensive failure.
Trust matters as much as the technology itself.
Some decisions barely improve with additional data.
More and faster data improves every decision an operation makes.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente "not all of them do" — nem toda decisão melhora com mais dados.

items.q: What does the phrase "a museum of expensive software that nobody uses" suggest about a failed transformation?
options: The software was cheap but poorly designed
The technology will eventually be adopted
The investment is visible but produces no working value
The failure was caused by external competitors
items.why: Inferência: "museu" evoca objetos caros expostos e intocados — dinheiro gasto sem uso real.

items.q: What does "a number they did not calculate themselves" reveal about the human side of transformation?
options: Calculations are always automated in logistics
Senior leaders never review the data
Data quality is irrelevant to decision-makers
Experienced people distrust figures they did not produce
items.why: Inferência: aceitar um número alheio depende de confiança organizacional — daí a resistência dos experientes.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando a revisão da transformação digital. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, three years in, let me be candid about where we stand. Roughly half of what we invested has done exactly what we hoped — quietly. Nobody celebrates it, but the routing decisions are being made earlier, the warehouse forecasts are steadier, and the numbers people argue about have shrunk. That is the compounding half, and I want to protect it.

The other half is harder to talk about. We bought two platforms that, frankly, nobody logs into. The dashboards were built, the training was delivered, and yet the schedulers still keep their own spreadsheets. When I asked why, the answer was always the same — they don't trust a figure they didn't work out themselves. That is not a software problem. That is a data-quality and trust problem we skipped over.

My recommendation is simple. Stop signing off on new tools this year. Instead, we clean the underlying data and we earn the schedulers' confidence, one decision at a time. If we rush this to hit the board's timeline, we will just build a bigger museum. I would rather move slowly and have every number believed.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Emily describe the successful half of the investment?
options: Quiet, with compounding gains worth protecting
items.why: "That is the compounding half, and I want to protect it" — ganhos silenciosos e cumulativos.

items.q: Why do the schedulers still keep their own spreadsheets?
options: They don't trust a figure they didn't work out themselves
The dashboards were too expensive to access
They were never given any training
items.why: "they don't trust a figure they didn't work out themselves."

items.q: What does Emily recommend doing this year?
options: Match the board's timeline at any cost
Sign off on two more platforms quickly
Stop buying new tools and fix data and trust first
items.why: "Stop signing off on new tools this year. Instead, we clean the underlying data and we earn the schedulers' confidence."

items.q: What does Emily imply by saying "we will just build a bigger museum"?
options: The board wants a showcase of successful tools
Rushing will produce more expensive software nobody uses
The company should exhibit its technology publicly
items.why: Inferência: 'museu' retoma a ideia de software caro e intocado — apressar só amplia o desperdício.

items.q: What can be inferred about Emily's overall stance?
options: She is indifferent to the board's expectations
She regrets the entire programme and wants it stopped
She values believed numbers over rapid tool deployment
She blames the schedulers for the failure
items.why: Inferência: "I would rather move slowly and have every number believed" — confiança acima de velocidade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The whole programme hinges on the flow of information between the depots." A flow of information is…
options: the movement of data from where it is produced to where it is used
items.why: Flow of information = fluxo de informação: o percurso dos dados até quem decide.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "No dashboard is reliable if the underlying ___ is poor."
items.why: Data quality = qualidade dos dados: a base sem a qual a tecnologia não entrega nada.

items.q: Organisational trust is best described as…
options: the legal ownership of company data
the reputation of the brand with customers
the number of managers in a hierarchy
the confidence that lets people act on figures others produced
items.why: É a confiança interna que faz alguém aceitar um número que não calculou — tema central da lição.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Leaders wanted results in one quarter, but the project demanded ___."
items.why: Long patience = longa paciência: transformações de logística levam anos, não trimestres.

items.q: "The board asked for an honest assessment of our readiness." This means a judgement that is…
options: candid, even when the conclusion is uncomfortable
items.why: Honest assessment = avaliação honesta: dizer a verdade sobre a capacidade real, mesmo desconfortável.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de transformação digital. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the next phase of spending." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the routing platform depot by depot." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The schedulers pushed back on the new forecasts." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We bought the tools but never followed through on the training." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Cleaning the data first is what will move the needle on decision quality." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
